title: Definition
body_md:
A Mukai vector $v=(r,\xi,a) \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$ is positive if
\begin{enumerate}
\item $r>0$ or 
\item $r=0$ and $\xi \ne 0$ is effective or
\item $r=\xi=0$ and $a>0$.
\end{enumerate}
We denote a positive Mukai vector $v$ by $v>0$.

label: thm:BM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:BM}
Let $(X,H)$ be a pair of K3 surface $X$ and an ample divisor $H$ on $X$
and  $(X',H')$ be a pair of K3 surface $X'$ and an ample divisor $H'$ on $X'$. 
Then the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
$M_H(v)$ is birationally equivalent to $M_{H'}(v')$ if and only if 
there is a (contravariant) equivalence $\Phi:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$ 
such that $\overline{\Phi}(v)=v'$, where
$\overline{\Phi}:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ is the Hodge
isometry induced by $\Phi$.
\item[(2)]
Under the condition of (1),
we can choose $\Phi$ to satisfy that
$\Phi(E) \in M_{H'}(v')$ for a general $E \in M_H(v)$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro:bir-auto}
Let $(X,H)$ and $(X',H')$ be polarized K3 surfaces.
Let $\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$ be a birational
map, where $v \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and $v' \in H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ are positive Mukai vectors.
Assume that $\operatorname{Pic}(X)={\mathbb Z}H$.
Then there is a (contravariant) Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$ 
which induces $\varphi_*$.

label: defn:theta
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:theta}
Assume that $v$ is primitive and $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq 0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theta}
\theta_{v}:v^{\perp} \to H^2(M_{H}(v),{\mathbb Z})
\end{equation}
denotes the Mukai's homomorphism.
\item[(2)]
If there is a universal family
${\bf E}$ on $M_{H}(v)$, e.g.,
there is a Mukai vector $w$ with
$\langle v,w \rangle=1$,
then 
$$
\theta_{v}(x)=
c_1(p_{M_{H}(v)*}
(\operatorname{ch} ({\bf E})p_X^*(1+\varrho_X) p_X^*(x^{\vee})))=
-c_1(p_{M_{H}(v)*}(\operatorname{ch} ({\bf E}^{\vee}) p_X^*(1+\varrho_X) p_X^*(x))).
$$ 
where $p_X, p_{M_H(v)}$ are projections
from $X \times M_H(v)$ to $X$ and
$M_H(v)$ respectively. 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
If $\langle v^2 \rangle >0$, then
$\theta_v$ is a Hodge isometry, where the lattice structure on
$H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z})$ is defined by Beauville-Bogomolov form.
\item[(2)]
If $\langle v^2 \rangle=0$, then 
$\theta_v$ induces a Hodge isometry
$$
v^\perp/{\mathbb Z}v \to H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z}).
$$ 
\end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{rem:BM2}
For the Mukai vector $u$ in Theorem \ref{thm:BM2},
we have a wall $W_u$ in the space of stability conditions $\operatorname{Stab}(X)$.
If $\langle u^2 \rangle=0$ and $\langle v,u \rangle=1$,
$W_u$ is a totally semistable wall, that is,
all objects are properly $\sigma$-semistable with respect to $\sigma \in W_u$.
Another type of totally semistable wall is defined by an spherical object
$F$ with $\langle v,v(F) \rangle<0$.
For this type of totally semistable wall,
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi$ which acts trivially on the Mukai lattice and
induces an isomorphism $M_{\sigma_-}(v) \to M_{\sigma_+}(v)$, where 
$M_{\sigma_\pm} (v)$ are moduli spaces of $\sigma_\pm$-stable objects such that
$\sigma_\pm$ belong to opposite chambers of the wall.

label: lem:lifting
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lifting}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be K3 surfaces.
Assume that there is no $(-2)$-curves on $Y$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
Let $f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(Y,{\mathbb Z})$ be an orientation preserving Hodge isometry.
Then there is an equivalence  
$\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(Y)$
such that ${\mathcal E}$ is a family of stable sheaves on $X$ 
and $\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces $f$.
\item[(2)]
Let $f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(Y,{\mathbb Z})$ be an orientation reversing Hodge isometry.
Then there is an equivalence  
$\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(Y)$
such that ${\mathcal E}$ is a family of stable sheaves on $X$ 
and ${\mathcal D}_{Y} \circ \Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}=\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[2-k]} \circ {\mathcal D}_X$ induces $f$.
\item[(3)]
Let $f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(Y,{\mathbb Z})$ be an orientation reversing Hodge isometry.
Then there is an equivalence  
$\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(Y)$
such that ${\mathcal E}$ is a family of stable sheaves on $X$ 
and ${\mathcal D}_Y \circ \Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces $f$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1)
Let $f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(Y,{\mathbb Z})$ be an orientation preserving Hodge isometry.
We take $u \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$ with $f(u)=\varrho_{Y}$.
Replacing $f$ by $-f$, we assume that $u>0$.
We set $X':=M_H(u)$, where $H$ is a general ample divisor.
Since $\langle f^{-1}(v({\mathcal O}_X),u \rangle=\langle v({\mathcal O}_Y),\varrho_X \rangle=-1$,
there is a universal family ${\mathcal E}$ on $X \times X'$.
Let $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$ be an equivalence
such that $\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}(u)=\varrho_{X'}$.
                                      
                                                            
Since $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$ is orientation preserving (\cite{HMS}),
$\varphi:=\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}} \circ f^{-1}$ is
also orientation preserving. Thus
$\varphi:H^*(Y,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ is an orientation preserving Hodge isometry
such that 
$\varphi(\varrho_Y)=\varphi_{X'}$ and
$\varphi(v({\mathcal O}_Y))=v({\mathcal O}_{X'}(D))$ $(D \in \operatorname{NS}(X'))$.
Replacing ${\mathcal E}$ by ${\mathcal E}(D)$,
we get $\varphi(v({\mathcal O}_Y))=v({\mathcal O}_{X'})$.
Then we have a Hodge isometry
$H^2(Y,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^2(X',{\mathbb Z})$ preserving positive cone, 
which shows that $Y \cong X'$.
                                                                                  
Since there is no $(-2)$-curves on $Y$, $\varphi$ is induced by an isomorphism
$\psi:Y \to X'$.
Thus ${\mathcal E}_1:=(1_X \times \psi)^*({\mathcal E})$
defines a desired Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}_1^{\vee}}$.
\begin{NB}
$\Phi_{X \to Y}^{{\mathcal E}_1^{\vee}}=\psi^* \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$.
\end{NB}

(2)
Since $f \circ \overline{\mathcal D}_{X}$ is orientation preserving, the claim follows from (1).

(3)
Since $\overline{\mathcal D}_Y \circ f$ is orientation preserving, 
the claim also follows from (1).

body_md:
\label{defn:B-stable}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
A $\sigma$-semi-stable object $E$ of phase $\phi$ is
an object of  ${\mathcal P}_\sigma(\phi)$.
If $E$ is a simple object of ${\mathcal P}_\sigma(\phi)$, then
$E$ is $\sigma$-stable. 
\item[(2)]
For $v \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$,
we denote the moduli stack of $\sigma$-semi-stable objects $E$ with 
$v(E)=v$ by ${\mathcal M}_\sigma(v)$,
where we usually choose 
$\phi:=\mathrm{Im}(\log Z_\sigma(v))/\pi \in (-1,1]$.
\end{enumerate}

\in {\mathbb R}_{\leq 0} \right. \right\},

where $\Delta(X)$ is the set of  $(-2)$-vector of $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:U_pm}
Let ${\mathcal E}$ be the universal family of stable sheaves with the Mukai vector $v_0$.
By \cite[Lem. 1.2]{Y:Stability}, we can choose ${\mathcal E}$ to satisfy one of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
${\mathcal E}$ is a family of $\mu$-stable sheaves or 
\item
${\mathcal E}=\ker(E_0 \otimes E_0^{\vee} \to {\mathcal O}_\Delta)$, where
$E_0$ is a $\mu$-stable locally free sheaf with 
$\langle v(E_0)^2 \rangle=-2$.
\end{enumerate}
For the second case,
$\Psi:=\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}} \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$
induces an isomorphism
$$
M_H(v_0) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } M_{(\gamma+sH,tH)}(v_0),\;
(s,t) \in U_+^\gamma.
$$
In particular we may assume that ${\mathcal E}_1^{\vee}=\Psi({\mathcal E})$.
Then we have $\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}_1}=\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}} \circ \Psi^{-1}$
and $\Psi$ acts trivially on the Mukai lattice.

body_md:
\label{prop:G-chamber}
Let 
$$
v=r+\xi+a \varrho_X,
$$
be a Mukai vector with $r>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Assume that $((\xi-r \gamma-rsH)\cdot H)>0$. Then
$$
{\mathcal M}_{(\gamma+sH,tH)}(v)={\mathcal M}_H(v)
$$
if $t \gg 0$.
\item
Assume that $((\xi-r \gamma-rsH)\cdot H)<0$.
$$
{\mathcal M}_{(\gamma+sH,tH)}(v)=\{F \mid F^{\vee} \in {\mathcal M}_H(v^{\vee}) \}
$$
if $t \gg 0$.

body_md:
\label{cor:G-chamber}
Assume that $((\xi-r \gamma)\cdot H)>0$ or
$((\xi-r \gamma)\cdot H)<0$ and $\theta_v(h_v) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$.
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X)$ 
such that $\overline{\Psi}$ acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Psi$ induces an isomorphism 
${\mathcal M}_H(v) \to {\mathcal M}_{(\gamma+sH,tH)}(v)$
up to codimension 1, if $|s| \ll 1$ and $t \gg 0$.

title: Example
body_md:
We set $v=(r,0,a)$ and assume that $0<-a<r$.
If $a=-1,-2$, then $\theta_v(h_v) \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$
Assume that $a<-2$.
For a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(r,0,a)$, we have an exact sequence
\begin{equation}
0 \to F \to E \to {\mathcal O}_X^{\oplus (r+a)} \to 0,
\end{equation}
where $F$ is a $\mu$-stable locally free sheaf.
For a general $E' \in {\mathcal M}_{(sH,tH)}(r,0,a)$, we have an exact sequence
\begin{equation}
0 \to  {\mathcal O}_X^{\oplus (r+a)} \to E' \to F \to 0,
\end{equation}
and $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta [1]}(E')=F$ and $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta [1]}(F)=E$.
Then $\Psi:=\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta [1]} \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta [1]}$
satisfies the required properties.

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof is similar to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:a>0}.
\begin{NB}
We set 
$$
v'':=-v'=r''+\xi''+a'' \varrho_{X'}.
$$

\begin{equation}
r''=-a_\gamma r_0,\; \xi''=-a_\gamma r_0\gamma'+r\widehat{\delta}.
\end{equation}

$$
\langle D_{v',\gamma'},\varrho_{X'} \rangle=a_\gamma r_0<0.
$$
Hence
$\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)) \cap L$ is spanned by
$h_v$ and $xh_v-D_{v,\gamma}$.

\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
-f(h_v)=& h_{v''}-\frac{(\delta \cdot H)}{a_\gamma}(-D_{v',\gamma'}),\\
-f(D_{v,\gamma})=& -(-D_{v',\gamma'}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
\end{NB}
(1)
Assume that $\theta_v(h_v) \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$
and
$(\delta \cdot H) \leq 0$.
The representation matrix of $f$ satisfies
$$
\det \begin{pmatrix}
1 & 0\\
-\frac{(\delta \cdot H)}{a_\gamma} & -1
\end{pmatrix}=-1
$$
by Lemma \ref{lem:Phi(h)2}.
Hence we get
$\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}+\epsilon D_{v',\gamma'}) \not \in -f(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H}(v)))$
$(0<\epsilon \ll 1)$.


(2)
Assume that $\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}) \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.
Since $\langle -f(h_v+\epsilon D_{v,\gamma}),\varrho_{X'} \rangle<0$
for $0<\epsilon \ll 1$,
$-f(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))) \not \subset \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.

\det \begin{pmatrix}
-1 & 0\\
\frac{(\delta \cdot H)}{a_\gamma} & 1
\end{pmatrix}=-1.
$$
By Lemma \ref{lem:mov}, we get
$\theta_{v''}(h_{v''}) \not \in -\overline{\mathcal D} \circ f(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)))$.
Hence
$-\overline{\mathcal D} \circ f(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))) \not \subset \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v''))$.

\begin{NB}
$\langle \Phi^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}_{X \to X'}(xh_v+D_\gamma),\varrho_{X'} \rangle=
-\left(\frac{(\delta \cdot H)}{a}x +1 \right)a_\gamma r_0<0$, if $x<0$
\end{NB}

(2)
Assume that $\theta_{v''}(h_{v''}) \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v''))$
and $(\delta \cdot H)<0$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:D*Phi(h)}, Lemma \ref{lem:mov} implies
$-\overline{\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ f(h_v)$ is not movable.
Therefore the claim holds.
\begin{NB}
$\langle -\overline{\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ f (h_v),\varrho_{X'} \rangle=r_0 (\delta \cdot H)<0$.
\end{NB}

label: lem:r_0=0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:r_0=0}
Assume that
$v_0=(0,\eta,a_0)$.
Then $\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[1]}(-e^{\frac{a_0}{(\eta \cdot H)}H}+m(0,0,1))$ 
$(m \gg 0)$
defines an ample ${\mathbb Q}$-divisor on $X'$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X)$ be an equivalence
such that $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}(E)=\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta}(E(nH))$.
We take a sufficiently large integer $n$ such that
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}$ induces
an isomorphism
$M_H(v_0) \to M_{H}(v_1)$,
where $v_1=(a_0+n(\eta \cdot H),-\eta,0)$.
We may assume that $M_H(v_1)$ consists of $\mu$-stable locally free sheaves.
Then the kernel ${\mathcal F}$ of the Fourier-Mukai transform 
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)} \circ \Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$
is a family of $\mu$-stable locally free sheaves with respect to $H$
(\cite{Y:Stability}). Thus
        
                                           
                                                                                             
                                                                                              
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal F}_{|X \times \{x' \}}=\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta}({\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}}(nH)),\; x' \in X'.
\end{equation}
\begin{NB}
$v({\mathcal F}_{|X \times \{ x' \}})=(a+n(\eta \cdot H),-\eta,0)$.
\end{NB}
We note that
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
&\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta^{\vee}}((0,(a_0+n(\eta \cdot H))H,-(\eta \cdot H)))e^{-nH}\\
=& (-(\eta \cdot H),-a_0 H,(\eta \cdot H)n^2(H^2)/2+a_0 n(H^2))\\
=& -(\eta \cdot H) e^{\frac{a_0}{(\eta \cdot H)}H}+
\frac{(a_0+n(\eta \cdot H))^2}{2(\eta \cdot H)}(H^2)(0,0,1).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since $\theta_{v_1}((0,(a_0+n(\eta \cdot H))H,-(\eta \cdot H)))$ is ample,
we get our result.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Let $M_H(v_0) \to M_H(v_1)$ be the isomorphism
in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:r_0=0}.
Under the identification
$H^2(M_H(v_1),{\mathbb Q}) \cong H^2(M_H(v_0),{\mathbb Q})$,
 $\theta_{v_1}(e^\gamma H)=\theta_{v_0}(\zeta)$, where 
$\gamma=-\frac{\eta}{a_0+n(\eta \cdot H)}$.

label: prop:FM1
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ preserves the orientation,
\eqref{eq:mov1} implies $\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}(v)=v'>0$.
We first assume that $r_0>0$.
We set 
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
v= & e^\gamma (r+r \delta+a_\gamma \varrho_X)\\
v'=& (-1)^k e^{-\gamma'}(a_\gamma r_0-r \widehat{\delta}+r/r_0 \varrho_{X'}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
If $(\delta \cdot H)<0$, then \eqref{eq:mov1}, Lemma \ref{lem:a>0} and Lemma \ref{lem:a<0} imply 
$\theta_v(h_v) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$.
If $(-1)^k (\delta \cdot H)>0$, then \eqref{eq:mov1}, Lemma \ref{lem:a>0} and Lemma \ref{lem:a<0}
imply 
$\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.
If $(\delta \cdot H)=0$, then $0<\langle v^2 \rangle =r^2 (\delta^2) -2r a_\gamma \leq -2r a_\gamma$.
Hence $a_\gamma<0$ and we get 
$\theta_v(h_v) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$ and $\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$
by \eqref{eq:mov1} and Lemma \ref{lem:a<0}.


We take a path $I:[0,1] \to U_-^\gamma$ such that
(i) $I(\lambda):=(s_\lambda,t_\lambda)$ with $0<-s_\lambda \ll 1$,
(ii) $I(0)=(s_0,t_0)$ $t_0 \gg 0$ and (iii) $I(1)=(s_1,t_1) \in {\mathcal C}_{-,0}^\gamma$.
By Corollary \ref{cor:G-chamber}, we get the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$M_{(\gamma+s_0 H,t_0 H)}(v)$ is isomorphic to $M_H(v)$ up to codimension 1 and
\item
$M_{(\gamma+s_1 H,t_1 H)}(v) \cong M_{(\gamma'+s_1' H',t_1' H')}(v')$ is isomorphic to $M_{H'}(v')$ up to codimension 1.
\end{enumerate}
 
In particular
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{(s_0,t_0)} \subset \theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))),\;
\Delta_{(s_1,t_1)} \subset \overline{\Phi}_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}[2-k]}(\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v')))).
\end{equation}
\begin{NB}
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Mov}(M_{(\gamma+s_0 H,t_0 H)}(v))=\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)),\;
\operatorname{Mov}(M_{(\gamma+s_1 H,t_1 H)}(v))=\overline{\Phi}_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}[2-k]}(M_{H'}(v')).
\end{equation}
\end{NB}
Then \eqref{eq:mov1} implies
$\Delta_{(s_0,t_0)}=\Delta_{(s_1,t_1)}$.
\begin{NB}
By our assumption and Lemma \ref{lem:f(xi)},
\begin{equation}
-a_\gamma h_v+(\delta \cdot H)D_{v,\gamma}=\lim_{(s,t) \to (0,0)} \xi_{v,\gamma}(s,t) \in \theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))).
\end{equation}
\end{NB}
Hence we may assume that $I([0,1]) \subset \xi_{v,\gamma}^{-1}(\Delta_{(s_0,t_0)})$, which 
means that all walls correspond to small contractions or totally semistable walls associated to 
$(-2)$-vectors by Theorem \ref{thm:BM2} (see also Remark \ref{rem:BM2}).
We note that $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a bijective map
$$
{\mathcal H}_-^\gamma \to {\mathcal H}_+^{\gamma'}
$$
which preserves chamber structures.
Then
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Phi:=\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$
with a commutative diagram \eqref{eq:comm1}.
\begin{NB}
\begin{equation}
\begin{CD}
v^\perp @>{\Phi}>> {v'}^\perp\\
@V{\theta_v}VV @VV{\theta_{v'}}V\\
H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z}) @>{\varphi_*}>> H^2(M_{H'}(v'),{\mathbb Z})
\end{CD}
\end{equation}
\end{NB}

We next assume that $v_0=(0,\eta,a_0)$, where $\eta$ is effective.
Let $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(v_0) \to M_{H}(v_1)$
be the isomorphism and
${\mathcal F}$ the universal family of $\mu$-stable sheaves
in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:r_0=0}.
Since $n \gg 0$, we may assume that
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(v) \to M_{H}(w)$
is the isomorphism \cite{Y:Stability}, where
$w=\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}(v)$.
By our assumption, we have an isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\theta_w^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H}(w))) \to
\theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))) \to 
\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))).
\end{equation}
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal F}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$M_{H}(w) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$, which shows
that $\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a desired birational map.

Finally we assume that $v_0=(0,0,1)$. In this case $X'=X$ and 
$$
\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[2]}(F)=F \otimes L, F \in {\bf D}(X),
$$
where $L \in \operatorname{Pic}(X)$.
Since $H$ is a general polarization,
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[2]}$ induces an isomorphism 
$M_H(v) \to M_H(v')$.
Hence we have an isomorphism
\begin{equation}
                                  
\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v'))) \to 
\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))).
\end{equation}
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[2]}$ induces a birational map
$M_{H}(w) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first assume that $r_0>0$.
We set 
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
v= & e^\gamma (r+r \delta+a_\gamma \varrho_X)\\
v'=& (-1)^k e^{-\gamma'}(a_\gamma r_0+r \widehat{\delta}+r/r_0 \varrho_{X'}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
If $(\delta \cdot H)<0$, then Lemma \ref{lem:a>0:2} implies $\theta_v(h_v) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$.
If $(-1)^k (\delta \cdot H)<0$, then Lemma \ref{lem:a<0:2} implies $\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.


${\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces an isomorphism
$$
{\mathcal H}_-^\gamma \to {\mathcal H}_-^{-\gamma'}.
$$
 
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:FM1},
we take a path in $U_-^\gamma$ connecting $(s_0,t_0)$ $t_0 \gg 0$ and $(s_1,t_1) \in {\mathcal C}_{-,0}^\gamma$ such that
all walls correspond to small contractions or totally semistable walls associated to 
$(-2)$-vectors.
Then
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Phi:=\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$
with a commutative diagram \eqref{eq:comm2}.

We next assume that $v_0=(0,\eta,a_0)$, where $\eta$ is effective.
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:FM1},
let $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(v_0) \to M_{H}(v_1)$
be the isomorphism and
${\mathcal F}$ the universal family of $\mu$-stable sheaves.
Since $n \gg 0$, we may assume that
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(v) \to M_{H}(w)$
is the isomorphism \cite{Y:Stability}, where
$w=\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}(v)$.
By our assumption, we have an isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\theta_w^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H}(w))) \to
\theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))) \to 
\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))).
\end{equation}
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal F}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$M_{H}(w) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$, which shows
that $\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[k]}$ induces a desired birational map.



\begin{NB}
We note that ${\mathcal E}^{\vee}[1]$ is a family of stable 1-dimensional sheaves with Mukai vector
$-v_0^{\vee}$.
Let $\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(-v_0^{\vee}) \to M_{H}(v_1^{\vee})$
be the isomorphism and
${\mathcal F}$ the universal family of $\mu$-stable sheaves. Thus
$$
{\mathcal F}_{|X \times \{ x' \}}=\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta}({\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}}^{\vee}(nH)[1]).
$$
                                          
Since $n \gg 0$, we may assume that
$\Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}:M_H(v) \to M_{H}(w)$
is the isomorphism, where
$w=\overline{\Phi}_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta(nH)}(v)$.
By our assumption, we have an isomorphism
\begin{equation}
\theta_w^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H}(w)))
 \to \theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))) \to 
\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))).
\end{equation}
Hence $\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal F}^{\vee}[k+1]}$ induces a birational map
$M_{H}(w) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$, which shows
that $\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}$ induces a birational map.
\end{NB}
If $v_0=(0,0,1)$, then the proof is similar to the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:FM1}.

title: Remark
body_md:
For the Mukai vector $v$ in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:FM2},
assume that $(\delta \cdot H) \ne 0$.
Then we have another formulation of Proposition \ref{prop:FM2}.
Let $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}_1}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$ be a Fourier-Mukai transform
whose kernel is a universal family ${\mathcal E}_1$ of stable sheaves with
$v({\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}}^{\vee})=r_0 e^\gamma$.
Assume that the cohomological transform preserves the movable cones:
\begin{equation}
-\overline{\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}_1 [k]}(\theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)))=\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))),
\end{equation}
 
where $H'$ is the ample divisor in \eqref{eq:polarization}.
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi_1:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Phi:=\Psi_1 \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}_1[k]}$ induces a birational map
$\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$ with a commutative diagram \eqref{eq:comm2}.
By Remark \ref{rem:U_pm}, these two formulations are the same. 
 
For example, assume that $\operatorname{Pic}(X)={\mathbb Z}H$ and
$v=(r,H,a)$ with $r,a>0$. Then 
$D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta}(E)$ is stable for a general $E \in M_H(v)$
but $D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta^{\vee}}(E)$ is not stable for all $E \in M_H(v)$.
Thus we need to take a non-trivial autoequivalence $\Psi$ for
the equivalence $\Phi$, which shows that $D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{I_\Delta}$ is also useful
(cf. \cite{FM118}).

label: thm:bir-auto
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:bir-auto}
Let $(X,H)$ and $(X',H')$ be polarized K3 surfaces.
Let $\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$ be a birational
map, where $v \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and $v' \in H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ are positive Mukai vectors.
Assume that $\operatorname{Pic}(X)={\mathbb Z}H$.
Then there is a (contravariant) Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi$ which induces $\varphi_*$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\varphi:M_H(v) \to M_{H'}(v')$ be a birational map.
By the work of Markman \cite{Markman} on the monodromy group, 
we have a Hodge isometry
\begin{equation}
\varphi_*:H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z}) \to H^2(M_{H'}(v'),{\mathbb Z})
\end{equation}
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\varphi_*(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)))=\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$ and
\item
$\varphi_*$ is extended to a Hodge isometry of Mukai lattices
$f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to  H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$ with
$f(v)=\pm v'$: Thus we have a commutative diagram.
\begin{equation}
\begin{CD}
v^\perp @>{f}>> {v'}^\perp\\
@V{\theta_v}VV @VV{\theta_{v'}}V\\
H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z}) @>{\varphi_*}>> H^2(M_{H'}(v'),{\mathbb Z})
\end{CD}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
$f$ is orientation preserving if and only if $f(v)=v'$.

(1) We first assume that $f$ preserves the orientation, that is,
$f(v)=v'$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:lifting} (1),
there is a Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$
which induces $f$.
We take an isotropic Mukai vector $u$ with $f(u)=\varrho_{X'}$.
We set $r_0:=-\langle u,\varrho_X \rangle$.
If $r_0=0$, then
there is a line bundle ${\mathcal O}_X(dH)$ such that 
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}(E)=E(dH)[-2]$.
                                          
Hence $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}[2]}$ induces an isomorphism.

Assume that $r_0 \ne 0$ and set $u=r_0 e^\gamma$. Then
$X'=M_H((-1)^k u)$ and ${\mathcal E}[k]$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
\begin{NB}
${\mathcal E}={\mathcal E}'[-k]$, ${\mathcal E}' \in \operatorname{Coh}(X \times X')$
and ${\mathcal E}^{\vee}=({\mathcal E}')^{\vee}[k]$, where $k=0,1,2$. 
\end{NB}
\begin{NB}
If $r_0>0$, then
$X'=M_H(u)$ and ${\mathcal E}$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
If $r_0<0$, then 
$X'=M_H(-u)$ and ${\mathcal E}[-1]$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
\end{NB}
Since $\rho(X')=\rho(X)=1$,
$\widehat{H} \in {\mathbb Q}_{>0}H'$.
By Proposition \ref{prop:FM1},
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi$ of ${\bf D}(X')$ acting trivially on the Mukai lattice
and
$\Psi \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$ induces the birational map
$\varphi_*:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$.


(2) We next assume that $f$ reverses the orientation, that is,
$f(v)=-v'$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:lifting}, there is a Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$
such that ${\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$ induces $-f$.
We take an isotropic Mukai vector $u$ with $f(u)=\varrho_{X'}$ and
set $r_0:=-\langle u,\varrho_X \rangle$.
If $r_0=0$, then the claim holds as in (1).
Assume that $r_0 \ne 0$, and set
$u=r_0 e^\gamma$.
$X'=M_H((-1)^k u)$ and ${\mathcal E}[k]$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
\begin{NB}
${\mathcal E}':={\mathcal E}[k]$ and $k=0,1,2$.
\end{NB}
\begin{NB}
If $r_0>0$, then
$X'=M_H(u)$ and ${\mathcal E}$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
If $r_0<0$, then 
$X'=M_H(-u)$ and ${\mathcal E}[-1]$ is the universal family of stable sheaves.
\end{NB}
We note that
$\widehat{H} \in {\mathbb Q}_{>0}H'$.
By Proposition \ref{prop:FM2},
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi$ of ${\bf D}(X')$ acting trivially on the Mukai lattice
and
$\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}$ induces the birational map
$\varphi_*:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$.
 
\begin{NB}
Then there is a (contravariant) Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$
which induces a birational map $\varphi$.
$\varphi_*(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))=\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.
We have a Hodge isometry
$f:H^*(X,{\mathbb Z}) \to H^*(X',{\mathbb Z})$.
\end{NB}

body_md:
We set
$$
A=\begin{pmatrix}
\sqrt{2} & -1\\
1 & -\sqrt{2}
\end{pmatrix},\;
B=
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & -\sqrt{2}\\
\sqrt{2} & -1
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Then 
$\phi_A(v)=v$ and $\phi_B(v)=-v$ 
$$
\phi_A(h)=\phi_B(h)=-3h+4\delta,\; \phi_A(\delta)=\phi_B(\delta)=-2h+3\delta
$$
where $h=(0,H,0)$ and
$\delta=(1,0,1)$.

$$
(\phi_A)_{|T}=(\phi_B)_{|T}=1_T.
$$

$\phi_A$ and $\phi_B$ define the same non-symplectic involution of $M_H(1,0,-1)$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:FM3}
Assume that $(\delta \cdot H) \ne 0$.
Let $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X')$ be a Fourier-Mukai transform
whose kernel is a universal family ${\mathcal E}$ of stable sheaves with
$v({\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}}^{\vee})=r_0 e^\gamma$.
Assume that the cohomological transform preserves the movable cones:
\begin{equation}
-\overline{\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \overline{\Phi}_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}(\theta_v^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v)))=\theta_{v'}^{-1}(\operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))),
\end{equation}
 
where $H'$ is the ample divisor in \eqref{eq:polarization}.
Then there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Phi:=\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$ with a commutative diagram \eqref{eq:comm2}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We set 
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
                                                
v'=& (-1)^k e^{-\gamma'}(a_\gamma r_0+r \widehat{\delta}+r/r_0 \varrho_{X'}).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
If $(\delta \cdot H)<0$, then Lemma \ref{lem:a>0:2} implies $\theta_v(h_v) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_H(v))$.
If $(-1)^k (\delta \cdot H)<0$, then Lemma \ref{lem:a<0:2} implies $\theta_{v'}(h_{v'}) \not \in \partial \operatorname{Mov}(M_{H'}(v'))$.

${\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}$ induces a bijection
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal H}_+^\gamma \to {\mathcal H}_+^{-\gamma'}.
\end{equation}
We take a path in $U_+^\gamma$ connecting $(s_0,t_0)$ $t_0 \gg 0$ and $(s_1,t_1) \in {\mathcal C}_{+,0}^\gamma$.
By our assumption,
we may take a path such that
all walls correspond to small contractions or totally semistable walls associated to 
$(-2)$-vectors.
Then
there is an autoequivalence $\Psi:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$
which acts trivially on $H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})$ and 
$\Phi:=\Psi \circ {\mathcal D}_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}[k]}$ induces a birational map
$\varphi:M_H(v) \cdots \to M_{H'}(v')$
with a commutative diagram \eqref{eq:comm2}.
